greek: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἡνίκα ἤρξαντο οἱ ἄνθρωποι πολλοὶ γίνεσθαι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ θυγατέρες ἐγενήθησαν αὐτοῖς.
hint: Men begin to become many, and daughters are born to them.

notes.text: Middle Liddell's first sense is *at which time, when*; *whenever* is its sense with the subjunctive.
*Began to become many*: ἄρχω with the infinitive, as at 2:3, and πολύς as the infinitive's predicate. The Hebrew is *hēḥēl lārōb*, *began to multiply*.
θυγάτηρ, *a daughter*, has one sense, so it is plain text.

greek: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων ὅτι καλαί εἰσιν, ἔλαβον ἑαυτοῖς γυναῖκας ἀπὸ πασῶν, ὧν ἐξελέξαντο.
hint: Rahlfs's apparatus records 'angels' for 'sons' in Codex Alexandrinus.

notes.text: *The sons of God*, Hebrew *bĕnê-hāʾĕlōhîm*, word for word. [[flag]] Rahlfs's apparatus records ἄγγελοι, *angels*, for υἱοί in Codex Alexandrinus, under the siglum A^r. The same phrase returns at 6:4, where the apparatus gives no variant.
καλός, *beautiful*; the Hebrew *ṭōbōt* is *good*. καλός carries *good* only fourth, after *beautiful, beauteous, fair*.
*From all, whom they chose*: ὧν takes the case of πασῶν. ἐκλέγω, *to pick out*, in the middle *to pick out for oneself, choose out*; the entry's active glosses are left out.
*For themselves*: the reflexive, as at 3:7.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος ὁ θεός Οὐ μὴ καταμείνῃ τὸ πνεῦμά μου ἐν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα διὰ τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς σάρκας, ἔσονται δὲ αἱ ἡμέραι αὐτῶν ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι ἔτη.
hint: The Greek limits the saying to 'these men', and makes them flesh in the plural.

notes.text: οὐ μή with the aorist subjunctive, the strongest denial: *shall by no means stay*. καταμένω is *to stay behind, stay*, then *to remain fixed, continue*. The Hebrew verb, *yādôn*, is of uncertain sense.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bāʾādām*, *in man*, singular and without *these*. The Greek narrows the saying to *these men*.

*Because they are flesh*, διά with the articular infinitive. [[flag]] The Hebrew *bĕšaggam hûʾ bāśār* is *in their erring he is flesh*, or *since he too is flesh*; the Greek has neither, and puts σάρξ in the plural, *fleshes*.
120, as in the Hebrew.
Lower case, as at 1:2: the entry's first sense is *a blowing*, and *spirit* comes after *wind* and *breath*.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: οἱ δὲ γίγαντες ἦσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις καὶ μετʼ ἐκεῖνο, ὡς ἂν εἰσεπορεύοντο οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πρὸς τὰς θυγατέρας τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἐγεννῶσαν ἑαυτοῖς· ἐκεῖνοι ἦσαν οἱ γίγαντες οἱ ἀπʼ αἰῶνος, οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ὀνομαστοί.
hint: Two Hebrew words, nĕpilîm and gibbōrîm, are one Greek word: giants.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew has two words: *hannĕpilîm*, the Nephilim, who were on the earth, and *haggibbōrîm*, *the mighty men* of old. The Greek has γίγαντες for both. Middle Liddell's first sense is *the Giants*, *the sons of Gaia* — the mythological race — and lower case here, as the Greek has no capital.
ὡς ἄν with the imperfect, *whenever*: a repeated going in, and the imperfect ἐγεννῶσαν after it is repeated too.

The imperfect ἐγέννων, with the ending -σαν. [[flag]] The Hebrew *wĕyāldû lāhem* is *and they bore to them*: the women bear. In the Greek the sons of God stay the subject — *they begot for themselves*.

notes.lemma: οἱ ἀπʼ αἰῶνος, οἱ ἄνθρωποι οἱ ὀνομαστοί
notes.text: The Hebrew *mēʿôlām ʾanšê haššēm*, *of old, men of the name*. ὀνομαστός is *named*, then *of name, notable, famous*.

greek: Ἰδὼν δὲ κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ἐπληθύνθησαν αἱ κακίαι τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ πᾶς τις διανοεῖται ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρὰ πάσας τὰς ἡμέρας,
hint: The Hebrew's 'inclination of the thoughts' is not in the Greek.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *rabbâ rāʿat hāʾādām*, *the evil of man was great*, singular. The Greek has *the badnesses were multiplied*, in the plural. κακία is first *badness* in quality, then *cowardice*, then *moral badness, wickedness*.

notes.lemma: πᾶς τις διανοεῖται … ἐπιμελῶς ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρά
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wĕkol-yēṣer maḥšĕbōt libbô raq raʿ*, *every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil*. The Greek has *each one ponders in his heart carefully upon the evil things*: no *inclination*, no *only*, and ἐπιμελῶς, *carefully*, which the Hebrew does not have.
The adverb of ἐπιμελής, *careful, anxious about*, filed inside the adjective's entry, as ὀρθῶς is at 4:7.
πονηρός is *toilsome*, *painful*, before it is *wicked*, as at 2:9.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH* alone.

hint: Where the Hebrew has God regret and grieve, the Greek has him ponder.

notes.text: ἐνθυμέομαι, *to lay to heart, consider well, ponder*; *to take to heart, be hurt* is its second sense. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyinnāḥem*, *and he regretted*.
διανοέομαι, *to be minded, intend*, then *to think over*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyitʿaṣṣēb ʾel-libbô*, *and he was grieved to his heart*. The Greek has no grief and no heart.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *YHWH*; the Greek has ὁ θεός alone.

greek: Νωε δὲ εὗρεν χάριν ἐναντίον κυρίου τοῦ θεοῦ.
hint: The Hebrew's 'in the eyes of YHWH' becomes 'before the lord God'.

notes.text: χάρις: Middle Liddell's numbered senses open with *outward grace* or *favour*, then *grace felt*, *kindness*, *thanks*. Its unnumbered heading, *Grace*, is left out, as the summaries of μετά and διά are.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕʿênê YHWH*, *in the eyes of YHWH*. The Greek has no eyes, and adds τοῦ θεοῦ. ἐναντίον with the genitive is *in the presence of, before*.
Glossed again, first in this chapter.

greek: Αὗται δὲ αἱ γενέσεις Νωε· Νωε ἄνθρωπος δίκαιος, τέλειος ὢν ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ αὐτοῦ· τῷ θεῷ εὐηρέστησεν Νωε.

notes.text: γένεσις, the word of the headings at 2:4 and 5:1, in the plural. The Hebrew *tôlĕdōt* is the same word at all three.

δίκαιος is first *observant of custom and social rule, well-ordered*, and *righteous* second; τέλειος is *having reached its end, finished, complete* before it is *perfect*. The Hebrew is *ṣaddîq tāmîm*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew *bĕdōrōtāyw* is plural, *in his generations*. Codex Alexandrinus reads γενέσει for γενεᾷ, as Rahlfs's apparatus records.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾet-hāʾĕlōhîm hithallek-nōaḥ*, *Noah walked with God*: rendered *was well pleasing to God*, as for Enoch at 5:22 and 5:24.

greek: ἐφθάρη δὲ ἡ γῆ ἐναντίον τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ ἐπλήσθη ἡ γῆ ἀδικίας.
hint: The Hebrew's violence is, in Greek, wrong-doing.

notes.text: φθείρω, *to ruin, waste, spoil, destroy*, in the passive. The entry also gives the passive its own translation, *to go to ruin, perish*, which the chain carries.

hint: All flesh had ruined its way: a feminine noun with a masculine pronoun.

notes.text: *Was, having been destroyed*: the perfect participle with ἦν, a state already reached. καταφθείρω is *to destroy, spoil utterly*.
The aorist and the imperfect of φθείρω share this form. The aorist answers the Hebrew perfect *hišḥît*.
σάρξ is feminine; αὐτοῦ is not. The pronoun follows the sense, not the noun's gender. The Hebrew *darkô* agrees with *bāśār*, which is masculine.
[[flag]] The Hebrew has *ʾĕlōhîm*, *God*; the Greek adds κύριος.

hint: The Hebrew's 'end of all flesh' is, in Greek, 'the time of every man'.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *qēṣ kol-bāśār*, *the end of all flesh*. The Greek has καιρός for *end* and ἄνθρωπος for *flesh*. καιρός is first *due measure, proportion*, then *a vital part*, and of time *the right point of time, the critical time*.
ἥκω is *to have come, be present*: a present form with the sense of a perfect.
[[flag]] *ḥāmās*, *violence*, as at 6:11.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

greek: ποίησον οὖν σεαυτῷ κιβωτὸν ἐκ ξύλων τετραγώνων· νοσσιὰς ποιήσεις τὴν κιβωτὸν καὶ ἀσφαλτώσεις αὐτὴν ἔσωθεν καὶ ἔξωθεν τῇ ἀσφάλτῳ.
hint: The ark is a wooden box, of squared timber, with nests.

notes.text: κιβωτός, *a wooden box, chest, coffer*. [[flag]] The Hebrew is *tēbâ*, used only of this vessel and of the basket Moses is laid in. The Greek word also names the ark of the covenant, the Hebrew's *ʾărôn*: Hebrews 9:4 has τὴν κιβωτὸν τῆς διαθήκης, and Hebrews 11:7 and 1 Peter 3:20 this one.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʿăṣê-gōper*, *gopher wood*, a word found nowhere else. The Greek has *squared timbers*.
*Nests of young birds*: Middle Liddell files the word under νεοσσιά. The Hebrew *qinnîm* is also *nests*, the usual word for a bird's nest; the Greek renders it exactly.

The Hebrew *wĕkāpartā … bakkōper*, *you shall cover it with pitch*, repeats one root, and the Greek repeats one too. ἀσφαλτόω is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ gives one sense, *smear with pitch*, citing this verse, so it is plain text.
*With four equal angles, rectangular, square*: an adjective in the genitive takes *of*, as πονηρός did at 2:9.

hint: The Hebrew's window, or roof, is not here; the Greek has 'drawing it together'.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ṣōhar taʿăśeh lattēbâ*, *a ṣōhar you shall make for the ark* — a word for a window or a roof, found only here. The Greek has *drawing together you will make the box*, and no opening.
*To a cubit you will finish it from above*, as the Hebrew *wĕʾel-ʾammâ tĕkallennâ milmaʿlâ*.
*From the sides*, plural; the Hebrew *bĕṣiddāh* is *in its side*. πλάγιος as a noun, τὰ πλάγια, is *the sides, the flanks*.

The Hebrew is *taḥtiyyim šĕniyyim ûšĕlišîm*, *lower, second and third* decks. κατάγαιος is *under the earth, underground*, filed under κατάγειος. διώροφος is not in Middle Liddell; LSJ's one sense is *with two roofs or stories*, citing this verse. τριώροφος is *of three stories or floors*. One sense each, so both are plain text.

hint: The deluge is named here, in the word Matthew, Luke and 2 Peter use for it.

notes.text: The Hebrew *hammabbûl mayim*, *the flood, water*, set side by side, and the Greek keeps both. κατακλυσμός, *a deluge, inundation*, is the word of Matthew 24:38–39, Luke 17:27 and 2 Peter 2:5.

τελευτάω is first *to complete, finish, accomplish*; *to end life, to die* is its second sense, which is the verse's. The Hebrew *yigwāʿ* is *will expire*.
ὅσος, *as great as, as many as*, with ἐάν for ἄν: *as many as may be*. Perseus's opening Latin, *quantus*, is left out.

greek: καὶ στήσω τὴν διαθήκην μου πρὸς σέ· εἰσελεύσῃ δὲ εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, σὺ καὶ οἱ υἱοί σου καὶ ἡ γυνή σου καὶ αἱ γυναῖκες τῶν υἱῶν σου μετὰ σοῦ.
hint: The first διαθήκη in the Bible, a word whose first sense is a will.

notes.text: *Covenant*, Hebrew *bĕrît*. Middle Liddell's first sense is *a disposition of property by will, a will, testament*; *an arrangement between two parties, covenant* is its second. Hebrews 9:16 turns on the first: ὅπου γὰρ διαθήκη, θάνατον ἀνάγκη φέρεσθαι τοῦ διαθεμένου.
ἵστημι in its causal tenses, *to make to stand, set*. The Hebrew *wahăqimōtî* is also *I will cause to stand*.
πρός with the accusative, *toward* you; the Hebrew *ʾittāk* is *with you*.
μετά with the genitive, the pronoun as plain text, as at 3:6.

notes.text: *Two two*, a distributive, *two by two*. [[flag]] The Hebrew here is *šnayim mikkōl*, *two of every*; the doubled form is the Hebrew's at 7:9.

The headword keeps the lexicon's order.

greek: ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ὀρνέων τῶν πετεινῶν κατὰ γένος καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν κτηνῶν κατὰ γένος καὶ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν ἑρπετῶν τῶν ἑρπόντων ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κατὰ γένος αὐτῶν, δύο δύο ἀπὸ πάντων εἰσελεύσονται πρὸς σὲ τρέφεσθαι μετὰ σοῦ, ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ.
hint: The Greek adds 'male and female' again at the end.

notes.text: *According to kind*, the Hebrew *lĕmînô*. γένος is first *race, stock, family*, and *a class, sort, kind* late in the entry.
The present infinitive, middle or passive: the first sense, *to thicken*, in that voice. The entry's passive glosses, *to become firm* and *to be reared, grow up*, follow in the chain.
[[flag]] Not in the Hebrew of this verse, which ends *to keep alive*.
Two words for birds: ὄρνεον, *a bird*, and πετεινόν, *winged fowl*. The Hebrew has *hāʿôp* alone, and the Greek adds πάντων before it.

greek: σὺ δὲ λήμψῃ σεαυτῷ ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν βρωμάτων, ἃ ἔδεσθε, καὶ συνάξεις πρὸς σεαυτόν, καὶ ἔσται σοὶ καὶ ἐκείνοις φαγεῖν.
hint: Food 'which you will eat', where the Hebrew has 'which is eaten'.

notes.text: *Which you will eat*, the future of ἐσθίω, second person plural. [[flag]] The Hebrew *ʾăšer yēʾākēl* is passive, *which is eaten*.
βρῶμα, *that which is eaten, food, meat*, from the same root as βρῶσις at 2:9.
*For those*: the animals of 6:19–20.
